terminus.status: COUNTEREXAMPLE · ROUTING WITHOUT A SINGLE SWITCHER
terminus.source: 2014 Taipei detailed-plan document for the west side of MRT Yuanshan Station
terminus.sourceFinding: The plan describes several simultaneously managed movement channels: a taxi stand, a retained one-way lane, a continuous pedestrian open-space link, parking access, and multiple public/private land-management bodies. Its stated aim combines development flexibility with transport-system efficiency and pedestrian friendliness.
terminus.generated: Switching power should not be modeled only as a person or institution holding a switch. A network can be rerouted by changing the material/regulatory affordances of links themselves. New distinction: operator switching power (an actor actively connects/cuts/reroutes) versus infrastructural switching power (rules, land-use designation, lanes, paths, access geometry make some routes available and others unavailable).

quality.evidence: high for planned route/access configuration; low for observed post-implementation behavior

terminus.falsification: This is not evidence that switching is decentralized or successful in practice. It only shows that topology-changing capacity may be embedded in infrastructure/regulation rather than concentrated in one operational switch-holder.
terminus.next: test operator-vs-infrastructural switching distinction against a non-urban domain and an observed implementation case
